goal: Clean the current translate-stage ownership, keep the corrected waiting semantics explicit, move truly parallel translate work out of the serial TranslatePipe, and preserve the existing preprocess-driven dependency and submit gating model without adding compatibility wrappers.

corrected_conclusions: TaskGraph::WaitUntilTasksComplete does not begin as a raw OS-level wait. It first expresses completion through task-graph dependencies, but it still forms a synchronous boundary at the current call site because DispatchTranslatePipelineBatch does not continue until the generated completion condition is satisfied.

The main serialization point is not each translate task itself. The current serialization point is the lifetime of the TranslatePipe batch closure in VulkanSubmissionExecutorEntry.cpp, because TranslatePipelineRuntime::Dispatch ultimately waits for all translate and submit-assembly tasks before enqueuing SubmitInfo objects into the submission runtime.

SubmissionPreprocess already decides which segments can run in parallel and already carries fence and translate ordering through last_fence_event, last_translate_event, per-segment task_dependencies, and dependency_graph. The redesign should reuse that ownership instead of inventing a second scheduler.

Submit remains a serial control boundary by design. A submit cannot be issued until the current SubmitContext has all required translate work completed, so serial submit work and serial RHICommandList ownership still belong to the TranslatePipe-side serial control path.
observed_problems: TranslatePipe currently owns both serial control work and the end-to-end batch wait, so the pipe stays occupied while parallel translate tasks are already executing elsewhere.
Parallel-capable translate segments are dispatched as AnyThread tasks, but their batch completion is still collected inside the serial TranslatePipe closure, which reduces overlap for later batches.
The current structure mixes three concerns inside one pipe lifetime: parallel translate dispatch, submit-info assembly, and serial runtime handoff.
cleanup_pressure: Delete or inline transitional scheduling code instead of layering a new compatibility path on top of the current TranslatePipe batch closure.
Do not add a fake abstraction around TaskPipe. If a new load-balance pipe is introduced, it must own a real scheduling boundary rather than merely forwarding calls.
Keep preprocess as the single source of truth for dependency modeling; do not duplicate parallel-eligibility logic in translate runtime.

design_constraints: Follow docs/rules/Rule_Codex.md: no fallback path, no compatibility shell, no over-design, and validation must stay test-driven.
Use the strict-engineering style: latest-only implementation, no useless wrappers, and explicit ownership boundaries.

Parallel-capable translate tasks must not consume the serial TranslatePipe lifetime. If a dedicated load-balance TaskPipe is introduced, it exists to dispatch or coordinate parallel translate work only.
TranslatePipe remains responsible for serial control-flow semantics only: submit-context progression, serial RHICommandList ownership, submit gating, and handoff to submission runtime.

Segment parallelism decisions must continue to come from SubmissionPreprocess and its existing dependency data, including last_fence_event, last_translate_event, task_dependencies, and dependency_graph.
Validation may use only existing PowerShell test scripts under testscripts/windows/test_*.ps1. No ad-hoc one-off validation wrapper may be introduced.
Windows-side script execution must use PowerShell, and validation review should filter validation noise and focus on blocking error lines as required by Rule_Codex.md.

checkpoints.title: Clean translate-stage ownership before changing scheduling
must_be_true_after: The code clearly separates preprocess ownership, parallel translate execution, serial submit assembly, and submission-runtime handoff.
Dead or redundant glue that only exists to keep the old mixed batch lifetime alive is removed instead of wrapped.

The corrected semantics of WaitUntilTasksComplete are documented in code-adjacent design notes or implementation structure, so future changes do not treat it as either pure async fire-and-forget or pure raw wait.

checkpoints.title: Move parallel translate workload out of the serial TranslatePipe
must_be_true_after: Parallel-capable segment translate work no longer occupies the serial TranslatePipe closure for the duration of its execution.
A dedicated load-balance scheduling path exists only for parallel translate work and does not become a second monolithic serial controller.
Translate task dispatch still respects preprocess-provided task_dependencies and queue/resource ordering.

checkpoints.title: Keep serial TranslatePipe responsibilities narrow and explicit
must_be_true_after: TranslatePipe handles only serial control duties: current SubmitContext progression, serial RHICommandList work, submit gating, and runtime handoff.
SubmitInfo assembly happens only after the required translate results for the current submit context are complete.
The serial control path remains compatible with the existing requirement that submit cannot happen until the current submit context's translate tasks are finished.

checkpoints.title: Preserve preprocess as the sole dependency authority
must_be_true_after: SubmissionPreprocess remains the single owner of segment parallel eligibility and fence ordering decisions.
No duplicate dependency classifier is added inside translate runtime or the new load-balance path.
Existing dependency carriers such as task_dependencies, dependency_graph, last_translate_event, and last_fence_event continue to define ordering.

checkpoints.title: Validate with existing PowerShell scripts only
must_be_true_after: Implementation validation uses existing testscripts/windows/test_rhi_translate.ps1 and, when integration scope expands, testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1.
No new primary test wrapper or ad-hoc verification script is introduced.
If the final behavior still lacks direct automation coverage, that gap is stated explicitly instead of being hidden behind manual claims.

execution_order: CP-01: remove mixed ownership first and make the corrected wait boundary explicit before reshaping scheduling.
CP-02: extract parallel translate work into a dedicated load-balance path so parallel-capable tasks stop occupying TranslatePipe lifetime.
CP-03: narrow TranslatePipe to serial control responsibilities and keep submit gating tied to current SubmitContext completion.
CP-04: re-check that preprocess remains the only dependency authority and delete any duplicated scheduling logic introduced during refactor.
CP-05: validate through existing PowerShell scripts only, with test_rhi_translate.ps1 first and test_all.ps1 as the broader integration pass when needed.

execution_result.validation_gap: Linux runner can invoke PowerShell, but the repository test flow currently expects a configured build directory, Windows-style executable layout, and this environment also fails CMake configure on missing X11. Existing scripts were attempted, but full checkpoint validation could not complete on this runner.

validation: Run PowerShell on Windows as required by Rule_Codex.md.
Primary validation path for this work: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\windows\test_rhi_translate.ps1
If the implementation changes broader executor/runtime integration, also run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\windows\test_all.ps1
When reviewing logs, filter validation noise and focus on blocking error lines rather than non-fatal validation chatter.
If no existing test_xx.ps1 script fully covers the final scheduling behavior, state that coverage gap explicitly.
